headline: Cedar Ridge site-wide punctuality collapse — third occurrence this month
narrative: On-time arrival at Cedar Ridge fell to 59.3% against an 88.9% trailing same-weekday baseline, affecting 978 trips. All five vendors serving the site were hit within a 7-point band (56.0% to 63.0%), so this is a site event rather than a vendor failure and no vendor penalty is warranted. Traffic-attributed delays tripled to 10.1% from a 3.4% norm. This is the third Tuesday/Wednesday occurrence in 14 days, following 8 July and 15 July, and Cedar Ridge now runs 73.4% on Tuesdays against 87.1% on Mondays.

trend.statement: Third occurrence in 14 days, deepening each time

peer.statement: Worst site-day in the business unit this month

threshold.statement: Below the 80% on-time target for the fourth time this month

impact.statement: 398 employees arrived more than 15 minutes late

recommendation.action: Add 10 minutes to planned duration for Tuesday and Wednesday Cedar Ridge routes, and open a joint route review with all five vendors
recommendation.expected_effect: On-time arrival rises from 81.5% to 90.4% across the business unit
recommendation.assumption: Recomputed against the same trip distribution. This moves the metric, not the commute — pair it with a journey-time fix or it is the same schedule padding Santa Clara used on 19 July.

headline: Santa Clara's 16.5-point punctuality gain is schedule padding, not improvement
narrative: On-time arrival at Santa Clara rose from 35.8% to 52.3% on 19 July. It is not an improvement. Planned trip duration rose from 40.6 to 58.1 minutes, up 43%, while actual journey time went from 76.4 to 77.0 minutes — six seconds longer. Planned distance is unchanged at 20.2 km and the site ran 14 fewer cabs. The entire gain came from moving the finish line 17.5 minutes later. Employees are spending exactly as long in the cab as they were before.

trend.statement: Step change on 19 July, sustained for 13 days

peer.statement: No other site changed its planned durations in this window

threshold.statement: Planned-to-actual gap now 18.9 minutes against a 5-minute fleet norm

impact.statement: 5,700 trips reported as on-time improvement with no change in employee experience

recommendation.action: Reject the reported improvement in the July site report and restate Santa Clara on the May planning baseline
recommendation.expected_effect: Reported on-time returns to 35.8%, the comparable figure
recommendation.assumption: Recomputed against the pre-19-July planned durations on the same trips.

headline: The unit raising the most severe safety alerts is the slowest to answer them
narrative: catalyst-Sac raised 23 Sev-1 alerts on 15 July against a 7.2 daily baseline, 11 of them over-speeding. The unit's mean acknowledgement time is 993.3 minutes — over 16 hours — and it has not moved in three months (965.2, 914.7, 993.3). orbit-Slc answers the same alert types in 3.4 minutes and vanta-Aus in 4.6. This is a 282-fold governance gap inside one organisation on one platform, and the fix already exists internally.

trend.statement: Flat for three months while alert volume grew 41%

peer.statement: Slowest of five business units by a factor of 282

impact.statement: 3,140 alerts a month acknowledged after an average of 16.6 hours

recommendation.action: Replicate the orbit-Slc alert triage process at catalyst-Sac; they answer the same alert types 282x faster on the same platform
recommendation.expected_effect: Acknowledgement time falls toward the 13.9-minute fleet median
recommendation.assumption: Assumes the gap is process rather than staffing. orbit-Slc handles 359 alerts a month against catalyst-Sac's 3,140, so headcount must be checked before committing to the target.
